task.title: Aggressive Tidy Memories with reviewed low-value removal
task.source: Direct user request after Tidy Memories retained junk singleton memories.
task.classification: memory cleanup prompt, review consent, and recoverable storage lifecycle

coreClaim: Tidy Memories reviews every eligible in-scope memory for consolidation and low-value junk, starts every removal unchecked, and applies a selected removal as an atomic recoverable status transition with exact undo.
rootCause: The prior cleanup lane only analyzed similarity neighborhoods containing two or more records, so a low-value singleton such as a captured generic statement could never become a cleanup proposal.

inScope: Chat and canonical recoverable discard apply and undo

riskClaimMatrix.coreClaim: Only an explicitly selected singleton discard removes a memory from active recall, and undo restores the exact prior record and canonical index state.
riskClaimMatrix.riskType: prompt review plus persistent storage lifecycle compatibility
entrypoints: Memory Console -> Tidy memories -> Analyze memories
Character Editor -> Memories -> Tidy memories -> Analyze memories
currentPathsOrFormats: Chat memory rows embedded in chats with active or pinned status
Version 1 cleanup preview and apply request contracts
legacyPathsOrFormats: Chat rows with optional updatedAt and pre-existing supersededAt or supersededByMemoryId fields
Canonical rows with pre-existing supersededByMemoryId links
Existing keep_one, combine, and conflict proposal batches without an operation marker
positiveRowsTested: All eligible memories are placed in deterministic bounded value groups, including an oversized singleton
A generic heat-stroke statement normalizes to one unchecked discard proposal
Pinned, manual, and edited discard cards show their source labels
Chat discard creates no replacement and exact undo restores the original row
Canonical discard removes the lexical index row and undo restores it
negativeRowsTested: Mundane user preferences and character-specific beliefs are protected by prompt controls
Malformed discard source counts, winners, replacements, reasons, and unknown IDs are rejected
Discard remains unchecked even if malformed preview data marks it selected
Stale chat and canonical batches fail without partial mutation
More than 1,000 selected operations are rejected before storage

groundTruthFacts.description: Discard is a recoverable status transition to deleted, not a physical purge.
groundTruthFacts.evidence: Focused chat and canonical apply-and-undo tests inspect persisted rows before and after undo.

groundTruthFacts.description: Canonical active recall is backed by memory-index-rows and discard updates that index in the same atomic collection operation.
groundTruthFacts.evidence: The canonical discard test observes index count 1 to 0 on apply and 0 to 1 on undo.

userActionCopy.description: No backup is required for the normal reviewed action because Undo restores the record. For an optional external copy before applying, export the character with memories from Character Editor to a separate character-backup.json file outside De-Koi's data directory.
userActionCopy.destination: A user-selected folder outside the De-Koi data directory
userActionCopy.action: Export before applying selected cleanup changes

outOfScopeClaims: This change does not prevent junk from being captured initially.
This change does not claim every configured provider will make the same subjective low-value judgment.
This change does not physically purge discarded history.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: Candidate preparation excluded singleton records, while storage only understood operations with a retained winner or replacement.
contractLaneGate.producer: src/engine generation produces reviewed cleanup proposals; src-tauri persists selected proposals.
contractLaneGate.consumer: MemoryCleanupReviewModal, chat memory recall, canonical memory recall, and one-batch undo.
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: Every eligible record may be reviewed for value, but only explicit user consent may remove one from active recall, and both storage owners must restore it atomically.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: The engine creates sequential bounded value groups and strict singleton discard proposals; the hook forces discards unchecked; Rust validates the shape and records recoverable deleted history with stale-state guards and owner-specific undo.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: src/engine owns proposal meaning and ranking, src/features owns explicit consent, and src-tauri owns atomic persistence and undo mechanics.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not hide junk only in the UI or physically delete rows in src-tauri; proposal semantics belong in src/engine and durable lifecycle mechanics belong in src-tauri.
regressionProof: The generation suite proves whole-scope sequential value scans, low-value normalization, negative controls, and discard-first conflict resolution.
The hook and modal suites prove unchecked consent, protected-source labels, copy, and the selected-operation cap.
The Rust memory-maintenance suite proves contract rejection, both storage owners, stale atomicity, index updates, and exact undo.

positiveRows.claim: Every eligible source is presented to the value-review lane in deterministic bounded groups.
positiveRows.evidence: Entity and generation suites passed 43 tests covering complete coverage, ordering, size bounds, oversized singleton retention, and sequential model calls.

positiveRows.claim: Low-value removal requires explicit user consent.
positiveRows.evidence: Hook and modal tests pass with discard selected false, disabled Apply before selection, and successful apply only after an explicit toggle.

positiveRows.claim: Selected discard is recoverable in both storage owners.
positiveRows.evidence: All 15 Rust memory-maintenance tests pass, including exact chat restoration and canonical row plus lexical-index restoration.

positiveRows.claim: The complete repository remains buildable and its architecture boundaries remain valid.
positiveRows.evidence: The full frontend suite passed 2,401 tests; production build, typecheck, architecture, docs, storage-contract, discovery, changed-file lint and formatting, and Rust workspace check passed.

contradictionRows.claim: Valuable ordinary information must not be treated as generic junk.
contradictionRows.evidence: Prompt calibration tests require mundane user preferences and character-specific ordinary beliefs to produce no discard.

contradictionRows.claim: A model or caller cannot bypass explicit consent or mutate stale data.
contradictionRows.evidence: The hook overwrites discard preselection to false, Rust validates exact request shape, and stale multi-source batches leave both owners unchanged.

contradictionRows.claim: A discard cannot masquerade as consolidation or create a replacement.
contradictionRows.evidence: TypeScript and Rust contract tests reject winner and replacement fields; persistence tests assert created and superseded counts stay zero.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Existing combine and keep-one cleanup behavior remains intact.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Existing generation resolution and both storage-owner consolidation apply-and-undo tests pass.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Older cleanup batches without an operation marker remain undoable.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Undo treats only operation=discard as deleted and retains the existing superseded default for prior batches.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Prior optional timestamps and supersession chain fields survive discard undo.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Chat and canonical tests seed protected rows with prior metadata and compare the restored records.

untestedRows: A real configured provider has not yet judged the synthetic low-value and valuable controls in a disposable live owner scope.

ownedFacts.description: The previous candidate lane required pairwise similarity evidence and therefore could not review a singleton for junk value.
ownedFacts.evidence: The pre-change candidate preparation built only pair-based groups and the original generation path iterated those groups.

ownedFacts.description: Discarded canonical memories leave active lexical recall in the same atomic storage transaction.
ownedFacts.evidence: The canonical persistence test verifies the memory-index-rows count changes with apply and undo.

userActionCopy.description: The review card says 'Remove from active memories. Undo can restore it.' Discards begin unchecked. For an optional external copy, export the character with memories to character-backup.json in a user-selected folder outside De-Koi's data directory before applying.
userActionCopy.destination: A user-selected folder outside the De-Koi data directory
userActionCopy.action: Export before applying selected cleanup changes

manualBlockers.reason: Public-path tests prove the scan, normalization, consent, persistence, and undo contracts; subjective provider judgment remains a deployment follow-up.

verification.baselineEvidence: 449 frontend files passed with 2,401 tests; 15 Rust memory-maintenance tests passed; typecheck, production build, architecture, docs, storage contracts, discovery metadata, changed-file lint and formatting, and cargo check --workspace passed.
